finding.claim: /checkout charges a client-supplied total computed from request-provided price and qty, enabling arbitrary or negative charges.
finding.source: cart.js:4 POST /checkout, body items[].price and items[].qty

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, both client-supplied; no catalog lookup, no sign or bound check

finding.guards_checked: No server-side price lookup, no qty floor/clamp or sign check, no items shape/SKU validation. Sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13) performs catalog lookup, so this handler lacks the control. Upstream auth for req.user not visible in repo (UNCERTAIN).

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:4-7 has no catalog lookup, no qty/price bounds, no sign check, and no items validation; the total is computed from req.body at cart.js:5 and passed straight to req.payments.charge at cart.js:6. The only checked controls are in the sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:10-17), which is a separate route and does not guard /checkout. Upstream auth for req.user and the internals of req.payments.charge are not in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied price*qty with no validation, and cart.js:6 charges that total, so any caller who can reach POST /checkout can submit a negative or arbitrary total (cart.js:4-7). The attacker is whoever can reach the route, presumably an authenticated customer, not a role that already holds the power. Residual uncertainty: upstream auth middleware and any validation inside req.payments.charge are not visible, so the reachable-attacker assumption and absence of downstream bounds are unverified, though no control in the repo blocks it.

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 does not reject non-finite qty; NaN (missing or non-numeric qty) or Infinity (JSON 1e400) propagates into the charged total.
finding.source: cart.js:10 POST /checkout-v2, body items[].qty and items[].sku

trace.note: catalog.price(i.sku) with unvalidated sku; unknown-sku return value not visible (UNCERTAIN)
Math.max(1, Math.floor(qty)) yields NaN for undefined/non-numeric qty and Infinity for qty=1e400
charge issued with NaN or Infinity total

finding.guards_checked: Math.max(1, ...) clamps negatives and fractions for finite values only. No isFinite/integer check on qty, no SKU validation. Impact depends on payments.charge and catalog.price, not in repo (UNCERTAIN).

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js. Line 14 (Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty))) clamps only finite values, so NaN and Infinity pass through to the charge at line 16. The repo has no isFinite check.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (cart.js:12-16 match the claim), but the only party who can trigger it is the authenticated customer whose own card is charged (cart.js:16, req.user.id), and that customer can already set any total they like by sending a large finite qty at cart.js:14. The NaN/Infinity case therefore gives the attacker no new capability, and the remaining effect is a self-inflicted or malformed charge, which is a correctness bug rather than a security vulnerability.
